challenges.name: strings-terminators-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: sizes, terminators and truncation
challenges.description: Read each snippet the way the C compiler and library do: where does a string end, how many bytes does it need, and which lines are undefined behaviour?

questions.explanation: sizeof sku is the size of the whole array: 16 bytes, no matter what is stored in it. strlen counts the chars before the first '\0': "MUG-01" has 6. sizeof p is the size of the POINTER, not of what it points to: 8 bytes on LP64. p + 4 points at the '0' of "01" (pointer arithmetic from lesson 2.1), so strlen(p + 4) counts "01": 2.

questions.question: Which of these snippets have undefined behaviour? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: "TEA-500" needs 8 bytes (7 chars + '\0'), so strcpy into char[7] writes one byte past the array. A string literal must never be modified, and char *s = "..." points at the literal itself (on Linux it lives in read-only memory and the write gets SIGSEGV). char s[] = "..." is your own array that is merely initialized from the literal, so changing it is fine. snprintf with sizeof buf writes at most 8 bytes and always terminates: buf holds "Nguyen " (7 chars + '\0'), cut but valid. strncpy copies exactly 4 bytes ("TEA-") and adds no '\0' because the source is longer, so printf("%s") reads past the end of f.

options.text:
char buf[8];
snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", "Nguyen Thi");

questions.explanation: snprintf returns the length the WHOLE result would have had, without the '\0': 7 + 1 + 10 = 18. It writes at most sizeof label = 12 bytes, and the last one is always the terminator, so label holds the first 11 chars, "LM-1042/Bin". Because 18 >= 12, the caller knows the label was cut.

challenges.name: fix-label-field-copy
challenges.title: Make the label field copy always fit and always terminate
challenges.description: label_copy() copies one field of a shipping label (customer name, city, ...) into its fixed-size slot on the Lotus Mart label printer. Short names print fine. But for "Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao" in a 16-byte slot the label shows the name running into the next field, a 1-byte slot gets overwritten next door, and the printer service cannot tell that a name was cut because label_copy returns how much it copied. Fix label_copy so that it never writes outside its cap bytes (not even when cap is 0), always leaves a terminated string when cap > 0, and returns strlen(src) so the caller can detect truncation with ret >= cap. The test runner puts the slot in the middle of a bigger array filled with '#' and reports guard=broken if any byte outside the slot changed.

tests.name: A short SKU fits in a 16-byte slot
A 22-char customer name is cut to 15 chars + terminator, ret reports 22
tests.expected:
ret=22
text=[Nguyen Thi Phuo]
terminated=yes
truncated=yes
guard=ok

tests.name: Exact fit: 7 chars + terminator in an 8-byte slot
Empty source gives an empty terminated string
One byte too long: 7 chars into a 7-byte slot
A 1-byte slot only has room for the terminator
A 0-byte slot must not be written at all
